reasons: Classification is correct: the § 2(a) grant runs to "Client" only, with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no notice-based mechanism to add them, so the clause fails the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice) on a material term; § 15 permits assignment only to a financially responsible affiliate, not to an M&A successor, which is the second fallback element.

Redline is valid and directionally correct for the customer: it inserts affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf into the grant and adds successor-transfer language to the existing consent exception, reaching the preferred position without disturbing scope, term or other commercial terms.

Edits are close to the smallest change that achieves the position — the grant sentence is otherwise untouched and the § 15 change is a clause-level addition to the existing carve-out (the changed-character ratios reflect short source sentences, not a rewrite).

No double-flagging: revocability is correctly noted as already acceptable (term-based, breach-based cut-offs), so the finding is scoped to deviation rather than walk-away, and no unnecessary edit to § 2(c)/§ 13 was made.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the written-notice fallback.
